transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Ever since they changed everything at school, I feel like I’m not handling it well at all and my reactions to the stress are taking over my life. I just feel completely overwhelmed and like I can't keep going on like this.
When did these feelings of being overwhelmed start, and have they been happening continuously for at least two weeks?

It all started about five months ago, within just a few weeks of when they announced the school restructuring and reassigned my classroom. Since then, it has been happening continuously every single day, so it has been going on much longer than just two weeks.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, or do you find it hard to feel pleasure in things you used to like?

Yes, I really have. I've completely stopped enjoying my watercolor sessions and salsa nights, which used to bring me so much joy. Now, I'm just too drained to attend family get-togethers or even talk to my husband in the evenings.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just overwhelmed by stress?

I don't think it's a separate depression, because my sadness and exhaustion are completely tied to the constant stress from the school changes. I genuinely believe that if they eased up on these test-score demands or let me go back to my old teaching style, I would feel like my usual, optimistic self again.

This indicates an adaptive response to stress rather than an independent depressive disorder. The persistent, maladaptive reaction to identifiable stressors lasting more than one month, with significant emotional and behavioral symptoms impairing functioning, supports a diagnosis of adjustment disorder (F43.1).
